method: Read frozen task manifests and one E3b NX graph at a time with existing RestrictedReader; no new semantic analysis, model imports, GPU or graph regeneration
counts_definition: edges are graph edges; target nodes are unique direct target node IDs; files are source_file membership in the frozen fold0 train/val split. These are structural coverage counts, not changed predictions.
notes: E2 has none of the three new relation types. E3a contains only STATE_DEF_USE. E3b contains all three.
Topological new two-layer pairs/targets come from frozen Stage F full-task analysis, not recalculated split-specific inference.
Changing trained common parameters may change predictions in files with no direct added relation; no score or causal performance claim follows from these counts.
Constructor edges are within constructor execution only; they do not constitute constructor-to-runtime cross-function state summaries.
No independent human or compiler approval is inferred from existing Codex review.

frozen_hgt_aggregation_note.relation_wise_reducer: sum of attention-weighted messages: fn.u_mul_e followed by fn.sum
frozen_hgt_aggregation_note.cross_canonical_reducer: mean, grouped by destination node type
frozen_hgt_aggregation_note.active_canonical_selection: all G.canonical_etypes also present in edge_dict, not a per-file or per-node incoming-edge filter

source_evidence.detail: collect each canonical message_passing result by destination type, then reduce_dict_data
stack relation output tensors and apply backend mean along relation axis; no per-node nonzero-degree mask in this merge
aggregate then node-type output projection, residual skip, optional layer norm

implications: A validation file with no directly added relation edges is not guaranteed to retain the same logits.
Training with enhanced relations can update shared HGT/classifier parameters differently even for files without local added edges.

A new registered canonical relation can participate in the mean of its destination node type in the full fixed graph. Its relation-output tensor can alter cross-relation normalization even where a particular node has no incoming edge of that relation.
Thus sparse direct-edge coverage is a structural statistic, not a strict bound on nodes/files whose representation or prediction may change.
These code observations do not establish that any accuracy gain/loss or specific prediction change has actually occurred; such claims require measured paired results.
